title: Reverse an owned linked chain without copying nodes
prompt: Node owns its successor through unique_ptr. Reverse an acyclic chain and return its new owning head. Empty input is valid. Do not allocate replacement nodes; tests check values and node identity. Use at most 100 nodes in this exercise.

tests.label: Same node identity
tests.hint: Reuse nodes rather than copying values.

tests.label: Singleton
tests.hint: A one-node chain keeps its identity.

hints: Save head->next before changing that link.
Moving a unique_ptr transfers responsibility for releasing its node.
explanation: Each iteration moves one node from the unvisited suffix to the reversed prefix. Every node still has one owner. The starter prints 1 2 3 instead of 3 2 1. A vector plus std::reverse is simpler when linked-node identity is not required. A raw-pointer version can work, but must state who deletes each node; unique ownership makes that obligation visible.
